narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductContraindication R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicinalProductContraindication` is a hard breaking change in R6: the R4 resource is no longer present as a StructureDefinition and must be migrated into `ClinicalUseDefinition` constrained to the contraindication branch. Existing R4 instances using `resourceType: "MedicinalProductContraindication"` are not valid R6 instances without a resource-type and content-model transform.

## Scope
The analysis compares the R4 resource to the R6 successor representation in `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are intentionally excluded from findings.

## Main migration themes
Migration is not a simple rename. R6 adds a mandatory `ClinicalUseDefinition.type`, requires at least one `subject`, nests contraindication details under `contraindication`, changes several value shapes to `CodeableReference`, replaces the R4 inline `Population` datatype with `Reference(Group)`, and replaces the R4 therapeutic-indication reference with inline indication backbone content.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest risks are the resource identity removal, required/type-changed `subject`, loss of direct `therapeuticIndication` reference semantics, `otherTherapy` child renames and target changes, and the population representation change.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for dereferencing or preserving referenced indications, modeling population groups, deciding whether R6 modifier `status` can be safely dropped when down-converting, and selecting terminology mappings for new example/preferred bindings.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most disruption appears to come from consolidating several R4 medicinal-product clinical-use resources into a single R6 resource. A less disruptive design could have kept old resource aliases or compatibility profiles, but the local package evidence does not include the rationale for the consolidation.

## Follow-up analysis
A complete migration program should also review `ClinicalUseDefinition`, `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `Group`, `CodeableReference`, and the related terminology ValueSets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductContraindication` is removed as an R6 resource and its content must be transformed into `ClinicalUseDefinition` with contraindication-specific structure. The top migration concerns are resource identity, mandatory/type-changed `subject`, moved/renamed contraindication fields, and population/indication representation changes. Confidence is high for computable differences, with residual uncertainty about the official design rationale and preferred cross-version maps.
summary.migrationThemesMd: The change is a consolidation and remodel rather than a field-by-field compatible evolution. R4 top-level contraindication fields generally move under `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`, several names change, CodeableConcept fields become CodeableReference fields, and R6 introduces discriminator constraints around `type`. Down-conversion from R6 to R4 is lossy for new targets, concept/reference alternatives, modifier status, group-based populations, library/applicability logic, and management/category metadata.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R4 resource is not present in R6 and that `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication` is the relevant successor, based on local package indexes, `fhir-old-types`, and the R6 StructureDefinition. Confidence is medium for exact business-safe transforms because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative migration guidance was available.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProductContraindication resource is removed and replaced by ClinicalUseDefinition

semanticText.definition: The clinical particulars - indications, contraindications etc. of a medicinal product, including for regulatory purposes.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators, serializers, and generated APIs recognize `resourceType: "MedicinalProductContraindication"`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition with this name; contraindication is represented inside ClinicalUseDefinition.

semanticText.definition: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect or warning for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `ClinicalUseDefinition` as the concrete resource. The old name appears in `CodeSystem/fhir-old-types`, not as a valid current StructureDefinition.

facts.note: Assigned R6 MedicinalProductContraindication StructureDefinition is absent.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition` explicitly includes a contraindication branch and describes the same clinical-use domain. The R6 old-types CodeSystem confirms the R4 resource name is no longer used.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break. A syntactically valid R4 resource with `resourceType: "MedicinalProductContraindication"` will not match any R6 core StructureDefinition. Generated classes, REST endpoints, search parameters, subscriptions, profile URLs, and reference-target checks that use the R4 resource identity must be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Contraindications are safety-critical; losing, misclassifying, or failing to load these records can affect clinical decision support and regulatory product information.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate several medicinal-product clinical-use resources into one ClinicalUseDefinition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated MedicinalProductContraindication resource alongside ClinicalUseDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating medicinal-product indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable-effect, and warning content into `ClinicalUseDefinition` is a coherent R6 modeling goal. The breakage is substantial because the R4 resource type disappears, but a compatibility resource would also create a long-lived duplicate representation of contraindication facts rather than a simple alias.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `MedicinalProductContraindication` as a deprecated or compatibility resource while adding `ClinicalUseDefinition` for new content. That would preserve most R4-valid instances, but implementers would need to handle two resource identities, duplicated search/reference surfaces, and potentially divergent profiles for the same clinical safety content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 payloads but leaves parallel same-domain resources, references, searches, and profiles to support indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a concrete resource named MedicinalProductContraindication.
R6 ClinicalUseDefinition covers contraindication among other clinical-use issue types.
evidence.quote: either an indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect or warning

evidence.detail: R6 classifies the R4 resource name as an old type.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative and omit unrelated optional metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: `MedicinalProductContraindication` no longer exists as a first-class R6 resource. Existing payloads, generated types, profile URLs, persistence tables, and API routes keyed by the R4 resource name require an explicit migration to `ClinicalUseDefinition`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance is R6-invalid solely because its resource type is unknown in R6. Conversely, an R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` contraindication is not an R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication` without a down-conversion that changes the resource type and remaps the content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit cross-version transform: change `resourceType`, set `type` to `contraindication`, move local fields under `contraindication`, remap subject and population, and update any references, search indexes, profiles, and persistence schemas that used the old resource type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation may be justified by a cleaner common model, but removing the old resource identity is maximally disruptive. A backward-compatible alias or deprecated compatibility profile would have let R4-shaped instances be recognized while steering new implementations to `ClinicalUseDefinition`.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R5/R6 migration notes if available; local package evidence strongly supports the successor identity but does not include design rationale.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 resource identity is gone in R6, so raw R4 instances, validators, generated classes, REST routes, and references keyed to `MedicinalProductContraindication` need an explicit migration to `ClinicalUseDefinition`. That is a real top-level break, but the R4 artifact was FMM 0/trial-use and the R6 consolidation has a coherent goal: one clinical-use resource with a type discriminator for indications, contraindications, interactions, effects, and warnings. The public IDMP context supports regulatory and safety relevance, but I did not find verified evidence that this exact low-FMM R4 resource has broad production dependence that would outweigh the consolidation rationale.
keyEvidence: R6 package index has `StructureDefinition-ClinicalUseDefinition.json` and no `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductContraindication.json`.
R6 `CodeSystem/fhir-old-types` contains concept `MedicinalProductContraindication`.
R4 maturity map: `MedicinalProductContraindication` is FMM 0, standards status trial-use.

R4 StructureDefinition description says the resource covers clinical particulars including contraindications for regulatory purposes; R6 ClinicalUseDefinition description covers indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect, and warning.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use substantially lowers the stability expectation, so removal alone is not enough for Revisit. Safety/regulatory domain relevance keeps the break important, but not enough to demand preserving the old resource identity in base R6.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the resource type, StructureDefinition URL, generated model, server surface, and reference target name change; raw R4 instances are also old-valid/new-invalid because the R4 `resourceType` is not an R6 resource.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated compatibility resource or alias would preserve many R4 payloads, but it would leave two base resource identities, duplicate searches/profiles/reference targets, and long-term same-domain maintenance. That is plausible but materially costly rather than a clearly low-cost alternative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact mechanics and partial alternative; the fresh judgment gives more weight to the R4 FMM 0 status and to the cost of retaining a parallel base resource.

findings.title: R6 requires a type discriminator and contraindication branch consistency

oldState.summary: No equivalent R4 discriminator; the resource identity itself implied contraindication.
oldState.narrativeMd: Every R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication` instance was a contraindication by resource type and did not carry a separate coded branch selector.

newState.summary: ClinicalUseDefinition.type is mandatory and constrained to match the populated branch.

binding.description: Overall defining type of this clinical use definition.

constraints.human: Indication, Contraindication, Interaction, UndesirableEffect and Warning cannot be used in the same instance
ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication can only be used when type is 'contraindication'

newState.narrativeMd: A migrated contraindication must set `type` to `contraindication`; branch content and type value are cross-checked by R6 invariants.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The discriminator replaces the semantic role formerly carried by the R4 resource type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A transformed instance that changes only the resource type but omits `type` or sets the wrong code will fail R6 validation. Runtime code must also branch on `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` rather than on resource class alone.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A wrong discriminator can cause a contraindication to be interpreted as an indication, warning, interaction, or undesirable effect.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow one resource to represent multiple clinical-use issue categories safely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `type` optional when exactly one branch is populated, or avoid it by retaining the old resource.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once R6 uses a merged clinical-use resource, an explicit required discriminator is a safety-oriented design choice because it prevents a contraindication from being processed as another issue type. A less-breaking inferred-type rule is plausible, but it is incomplete for empty or metadata-only resources and would make category handling less explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base design could have allowed `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` to be omitted when one branch, such as `contraindication`, is present and unambiguous. That would ease migration from a resource whose type already implied contraindication, but it adds validation ambiguity and makes indexing, search, and client branching depend on inferred structure rather than a mandatory code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces enrichment burden but weakens explicit classification, search consistency, and validation of branch/category mismatches.

evidence.detail: R6 `type` is 1..1 code with required binding.
R6 requires contraindication content to match `type = 'contraindication'`.

examples.examplesMd: The invalid example shows a partially migrated R6-shaped resource missing the mandatory discriminator.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 did not need a discriminator because the resource name carried the clinical-use category. R6 makes the category explicit and enforces consistency. This is easy to populate but easy to miss in mechanical migrations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data transformed to `ClinicalUseDefinition` without `type` is invalid in R6. R6-to-R4 conversion can usually drop `type = 'contraindication'`, but any other type is outside this artifact's R4 representation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Set `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` to `contraindication` for every migrated R4 contraindication. Add tests for missing `type`, wrong `type`, multiple branches, and valid single-branch contraindications.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This constraint is largely unavoidable in the merged R6 resource. The backward-compatible alternative would have been preserving the R4 resource identity as a separate compatibility entry point.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The required code system was not expanded, but the needed migration code is explicit in the StructureDefinition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: After migrating to `ClinicalUseDefinition`, R6 requires `type = contraindication` and uses error invariants to keep the populated branch consistent with the type. This is a validation break for a partial transform that only changes the resource name, but the value is deterministic for this R4 artifact and is safety-relevant in a merged resource where several clinical-use branches coexist.
keyEvidence: R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` is `1..1` code with required binding to `clinical-use-definition-type`.
R6 root constraint `cud-2` requires `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication` to be empty unless `type = 'contraindication'`.
R4 had no separate discriminator because the resource type itself identified contraindication.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Because the old artifact is FMM 0/trial-use, the added discriminator does not need the same compatibility burden as mature content. The low FMM combines with an easy deterministic migration to support accepting the break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a migrated R6-shaped instance with contraindication content but no `type`, or with the wrong type code, fails R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could infer type from the single populated branch or make `type` optional, but that would make indexing, client branching, and branch/type mismatch detection less explicit. A required discriminator is proportionate for the merged model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies the hard validation mechanism, but its high overall impact feels overstated for a deterministic required value on FMM 0 content.

findings.title: Subject becomes mandatory and changes from Reference to CodeableReference with different targets

oldState.summary: Optional repeating Reference to MedicinalProduct or Medication.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a contraindication without a `subject`, and when present the subject was a FHIR `Reference` to `MedicinalProduct` or `Medication`.

newState.summary: Mandatory repeating CodeableReference with broader but changed target profiles.

binding.description: A coded concept that defines the type of a medication.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires at least one subject and permits either a coded concept or reference through `CodeableReference`; the R4 `MedicinalProduct` target has been replaced by `MedicinalProductDefinition`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements identify the medication/product/etc. for which the contraindication applies.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The min cardinality increase is a direct validation break for R4 instances that omitted subject. The datatype change also breaks generated code and wire transforms: `CodeableReference` wraps references under `reference` and can carry concepts that R4 `Reference` cannot represent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A contraindication without a reliably mapped subject is clinically unsafe because the prohibited product or therapy may be unclear.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure every clinical-use definition identifies its subject and allow coded subjects as well as references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `subject` optional and retain an R4-compatible reference representation while adding coded-subject support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring a subject is clinically reasonable for contraindication knowledge because an unscoped safety rule can be unsafe or unusable. The CodeableReference expansion also has a plausible R6 goal, but preserving all R4 instances would require keeping optionality and an old reference shape, which carries meaningful safety and modeling tradeoffs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `subject` at `0..*`, kept an R4-compatible reference element, and added a separate coded or broader subject element for new R6 use cases. That would preserve old instances, including records with no subject, but it would reduce the assurance that every base R6 clinical-use definition identifies what it applies to and could leave multiple subject representations for the same fact.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves incomplete historical records but weakens a clinically important base guarantee and risks duplicate subject representations.

evidence.detail: R4 subject is 0..* Reference to MedicinalProduct or Medication.
R6 subject is 1..* CodeableReference with a different target-profile set.

examples.examplesMd: The first example illustrates missing subject; the second shows an R6 coded subject with no R4 Reference equivalent.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject` is both stricter and structurally different. Migrations must not simply copy the R4 `Reference` array; they must wrap each reference in `CodeableReference.reference`, translate `MedicinalProduct` references to `MedicinalProductDefinition` where possible, and supply a subject when R4 omitted one.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances without subject can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. R6 instances with `subject.concept` or targets outside R4's `MedicinalProduct|Medication` set cannot be represented losslessly in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory records missing subject and define a remediation policy. For present R4 references, wrap as `CodeableReference.reference`; map `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition` if a target migration exists. Test missing subject, medication reference, medicinal product reference, and coded subject cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter requirement is clinically reasonable but not backward-compatible. Profiles or warnings could have enforced subject presence for new data while still accepting historical records.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `subject` changes from optional R4 `Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)` to mandatory R6 `CodeableReference` with a changed and broader target set. Records with no subject require remediation, and present R4 references need wrapping and sometimes target-resource migration. Still, a contraindication without a subject is weak or unsafe clinical knowledge, so requiring at least one subject is a defensible R6 base requirement despite the break.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication.subject`: `0..* Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication)`.

R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject`: `1..* CodeableReference(MedicinalProductDefinition|Medication|ActivityDefinition|PlanDefinition|Device|DeviceDefinition|SubstanceDefinition|NutritionProduct|BiologicallyDerivedProduct)`.
R4 maturity map: FMM 0/trial-use.

Public IDMP context checked: clinical-use/contraindication data is described as patient-safety and regulatory relevant, but no verified source showed broad dependence on subject-omitting R4 instances.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM softens the compatibility concern, but the path is central to the meaning of a contraindication. The safety rationale for a required subject outweighs preserving incomplete FMM 0 records in the base model.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances that omit `subject` cannot validate after migration without adding one; runtime/API/codegen also changes because references are nested under `CodeableReference.reference`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `subject` optional or retaining a separate R4-shaped reference element would preserve more old data, but it would weaken the R6 guarantee that every clinical-use definition identifies what it applies to and could create duplicate subject representations. A warning/profile requirement would be less breaking but less safe as a base rule.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing hard-break and partial-alternative assessment; the fresh review accepts the change as proportionate because the old content is FMM 0 and the subject requirement has a strong safety rationale.

findings.title: Top-level contraindication details move under ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication with renamed paths

oldState.summary: Contraindication details were direct children of the resource.

newState.summary: Contraindication-specific details are nested under a 0..1 backbone selected by type.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 nests contraindication fields under `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`; for example, R4 `disease` corresponds to R6 `contraindication.diseaseSymptomProcedure`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element definitions and names preserve the contraindication semantics while moving content into a branch of the merged successor resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON paths used by R4 are not valid R6 paths. Generated models, FHIRPath expressions, database column mappings, search extraction logic, and validation profiles that refer to R4 top-level elements must be rewritten.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropped or misnested contraindication details can change the clinical meaning of a safety rule.

justification.inferredGoal: Organize contraindication content as one branch of the merged ClinicalUseDefinition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep old contraindication fields as top-level compatibility elements while adding the branch.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving details under `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication` follows from the merged-resource design and gives each issue type a clear branch. A base R6 model could have retained old top-level fields, but that would make contraindication the exceptional branch and create two places for the same facts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking option is not ordinary conversion tooling or extensions; it would require the base R6 resource to accept the old top-level fields alongside the new `contraindication` backbone. That would preserve many R4-shaped payloads after resource-type migration, but it risks conflicting branch and top-level values and a compatibility surface that may never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids path rewrites but duplicates branch and top-level representations and complicates invariants and generated APIs.

evidence.detail: R4 defines contraindication details as direct local children.
R6 defines a contraindication backbone with nested child content.

examples.examplesMd: R4 top-level elements must be moved under `contraindication`; additional datatype wrapping is covered in separate findings.

findings.narrativeMd: The local content did not merely stay on a renamed resource. R6 introduces a category-specific backbone, so path-based consumers must descend through `contraindication` to find the clinical facts.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-shaped payload with top-level `disease` or `otherTherapy` is invalid as an R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition`. A down-converter must flatten the branch back to R4 paths and reject or separately handle non-contraindication branches.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update transforms, FHIRPath, database mappings, search indexes, and codegen assumptions to the new paths. Regression tests should assert that all R4 local fields are present at their expected R6 nested locations after migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is structurally tied to the merged successor resource. A compatibility layer could hide this from API clients, but the core wire format remains breaking.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 contraindication-specific children move from the resource root into `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`, with `disease` also renamed to `diseaseSymptomProcedure`. This breaks FHIRPath, serialization, extraction, and generated accessors, but it follows directly from the R6 decision to make contraindication one branch of a broader clinical-use resource. Keeping the old top-level fields in base R6 would make contraindication structurally exceptional and duplicate the branch content.
keyEvidence: R4 direct children include `disease`, `diseaseStatus`, `comorbidity`, `therapeuticIndication`, `otherTherapy`, and `population`.
R6 defines `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication` as `0..1 BackboneElement` with nested contraindication details.
R6 `cud-1` prevents more than one issue branch in the same instance, and `cud-2` ties the contraindication branch to `type = 'contraindication'`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use makes a branch-level remodel more acceptable than it would be for mature content. The domain is important, but this particular path move is mostly structural and mechanically mappable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-shaped top-level fields such as `disease` or `otherTherapy` are not valid R6 fields on `ClinicalUseDefinition`; runtime/API/codegen paths also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Base R6 could accept old top-level compatibility elements alongside `contraindication`, but that would create two locations for the same facts, conflict rules, and extra generated API surface. A clean branch is proportionate once the merged resource design is accepted.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high path-break assessment and partial alternative; the fresh review weighs the structural move as a reasonable consequence of the merged model on FMM 0 content.

findings.title: Disease, diseaseStatus, and comorbidity change from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Clinical condition/status fields were CodeableConcept values without local bindings.
oldState.narrativeMd: `disease`, `diseaseStatus`, and `comorbidity` were coded concepts directly at their R4 paths.

newState.summary: Mapped fields are CodeableReference values, optionally referencing ObservationDefinition, with example bindings.

binding.description: Example bindings for symptom/disease/procedure and disease status.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can carry either a coded concept or a reference, using `CodeableReference.concept` or `CodeableReference.reference`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element names and definitions preserve the same condition/status/comorbidity meanings, with changed representation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Even after moving paths, a raw R4 `CodeableConcept` object cannot be copied as the value of a R6 `CodeableReference`; it must be wrapped under `concept`. R6 references to `ObservationDefinition` cannot be represented as R4 CodeableConcepts without dereferencing or losing identity.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect wrapping or failed dereferencing can obscure the actual contraindicating condition.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow clinical-use conditions to be represented by reusable definitions as well as codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain CodeableConcept fields and add separate reference alternatives for reusable definitions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing condition and status values to point to reusable definitions is a reasonable expressiveness goal, and `CodeableReference` is the R6 idiom for concept-or-reference content. A less-breaking base shape could preserve old CodeableConcept values, but it would be less uniform and would need rules to avoid competing concept and reference representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have kept the CodeableConcept-valued condition/status elements and added optional reference siblings for ObservationDefinition-based cases. This would preserve old values without wrapping, but it introduces the long-term risk of two same-fact representations and more complex validation or code generation than a single `CodeableReference` element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 concept values but loses the uniform CodeableReference pattern and may duplicate concept/reference forms.

evidence.detail: R4 fields are CodeableConcept.
R6 fields are CodeableReference targeting ObservationDefinition, with example bindings.

examples.examplesMd: R4 concepts generally map to `CodeableReference.concept`; R6 references need a separate dereference or extension policy for R4.

findings.narrativeMd: The condition/status fields are semantically recognizable but structurally different. Implementers must wrap R4 coded values in `concept` and decide how to handle R6 reference-based values when down-converting.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A migrated R6 instance with `diseaseSymptomProcedure.coding` directly is invalid; the coding must be under `diseaseSymptomProcedure.concept`. R6 `reference` alternatives are not cleanly R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform `CodeableConcept` values to `CodeableReference.concept`. If an R6 value uses `reference`, either dereference to a codeable concept, carry an extension, or mark the record as not losslessly down-convertible. Terminology validation should use the R6 example bindings where applicable, but those bindings are not required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A choice element retaining the old CodeableConcept shape could have reduced wire-format disruption, but CodeableReference provides a uniform R6 representation for concept-or-reference patterns.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `disease`, `diseaseStatus`, and `comorbidity` move from plain `CodeableConcept` values to `CodeableReference` values, so R4 concepts must be wrapped under `.concept` and R6 reference alternatives cannot always round-trip to R4. This is real migration work, but it is largely mechanical in the R4-to-R6 direction and matches the R6 pattern for allowing either a code or a reusable definition.
keyEvidence: R4 `disease`, `diseaseStatus`, and `comorbidity` are `CodeableConcept`.
R6 `contraindication.diseaseSymptomProcedure`, `diseaseStatus`, and `comorbidity` are `CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition)`.
R6 adds example bindings for disease/symptom/procedure and disease status; they are not required bindings.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the need to preserve the old raw `CodeableConcept` wire shape. Because R4 concepts have a straightforward `.concept` mapping, the low maturity pushes this toward acceptable migration burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: after the path move, placing a raw `CodeableConcept` directly where R6 expects a `CodeableReference` is invalid; R6-to-R4 loss occurs when the R6 value uses `.reference` rather than `.concept`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could keep CodeableConcept fields and add reference siblings, or define a choice, but that duplicates concept/reference representations and weakens the uniform `CodeableReference` model. The less-breaking design has meaningful complexity costs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies the type break and partial alternative, while the fresh review treats the R4-to-R6 side as mostly mechanical and proportionate.

findings.title: therapeuticIndication Reference is replaced by inline contraindication.indication content

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 linked a contraindication to separate `MedicinalProductIndication` resources.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `contraindication.indication` uses a `contentReference` to the `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication` backbone, not a FHIR `Reference` to another resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 definition says this is the indication which the contraindication is for; this matches the R4 therapeuticIndication relationship but changes it from reference to inline content.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Reference-valued R4 data cannot be copied into the R6 inline backbone. A converter must dereference linked indication resources or preserve unresolved links by extension. R6 inline indication details may lack a stable standalone resource identity to use as an R4 `Reference`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The indication context can materially alter interpretation of when a contraindication applies.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent indication context within the same clinical-use resource rather than relying on separate resource links.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Permit a reference-valued indication relationship as well as inline indication content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Inlining the indication context may support self-contained clinical-use definitions, but the supplied artifacts do not show why the old reference relationship had to disappear completely. Because indication resources may have their own identity, provenance, and reuse, the level of breakage is not clearly justified by the available evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have added an optional reference relationship, for example to an indication `ClinicalUseDefinition`, while also allowing inline indication content for self-contained cases. This is only a partial alternative because it would require rules for when inline and referenced indication data coexist and how conflicts are resolved, but it would preserve more R4 reference-based workflows than the current inline-only model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 link semantics but creates inline-versus-referenced duplication and possible conflict.

evidence.detail: R4 therapeuticIndication is Reference(MedicinalProductIndication).
R6 contraindication.indication is a contentReference to ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example assumes the referenced indication has been resolved and inlined.

findings.narrativeMd: The old relationship was a resource reference; the new representation is embedded indication content. This can affect both data integrity and referential workflows because the linked indication may have independent identifiers, provenance, or reuse.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 Reference object is invalid at the R6 inline backbone location. R6 inline content cannot always be down-converted to an R4 reference unless a separate R4/R6 indication resource is created and linked.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each R4 `therapeuticIndication` reference, decide whether to dereference and inline the target, create a companion `ClinicalUseDefinition` indication resource and use an extension/link, or flag unresolved references for manual review. Preserve provenance and identifiers where business processes depend on the referenced indication.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A reference alternative would have been more backward-compatible and less lossy. If inline content was required for self-contained clinical-use definitions, both patterns could have coexisted with invariants to prevent contradictory content.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 linked contraindications to separate `MedicinalProductIndication` resources, while R6 embeds indication backbone content inside the contraindication branch. That is more than a wrapper change: migration can require dereferencing another resource, preserving identifiers/provenance, and deciding what to do when the referenced indication is unavailable or reused elsewhere. Even with FMM 0, the indication context can be safety- and regulatory-relevant, and a reference-preserving R6 option looks plausible enough to deserve renewed design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 `therapeuticIndication`: `0..* Reference(MedicinalProductIndication)`.
R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication.indication`: `0..*` contentReference `#ClinicalUseDefinition.indication`.
R4 `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductIndication.json` is present, confirming the old target was an independent resource.

Public IDMP context checked: clinical-use data includes indications and contraindications for regulatory and patient-safety use cases, but no verified production dependency on this exact R4 reference path was found.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability expectation, but it does not erase the concern because this path can require lossy or expert-dependent migration of an independent referenced clinical-use fact.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `Reference(MedicinalProductIndication)` is not valid at an R6 inline backbone location; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs when inline indication content has no stable resource identity to reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could allow either inline indication content or a reference to an indication `ClinicalUseDefinition`, with rules for avoiding contradictions. That has duplication and conflict-rule costs, but it would preserve important link semantics and reduce dereferencing/manual migration burden.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high impact and partial alternative assessment; after fresh review, this is one of the low-FMM findings where lossy, expert-dependent migration justifies Revisit.

findings.title: otherTherapy child names and medication representation change

oldState.summary: Backbone with therapyRelationshipType 1..1 and medication[x] 1..1 CodeableConcept or Reference.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented related therapy using `otherTherapy.therapyRelationshipType` and choice element `otherTherapy.medication[x]`.

newState.summary: Content reference to indication.otherTherapy with relationshipType 1..1 and treatment 1..1 CodeableReference.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 reuses `ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.otherTherapy`. The child names are `relationshipType` and `treatment`; `treatment` is a `CodeableReference` with changed target profiles.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions for the old and new elements both describe the relationship between the indication/contraindication and another therapy.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The child names changed, the choice element disappeared, and target profiles changed. R4 `medicationCodeableConcept` and `medicationReference` cannot be copied to R6; they must become `treatment.concept` or `treatment.reference`, with target resource migrations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Other-therapy relationships can define interaction-like or conditional contraindication logic; losing the related treatment changes clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse a common other-therapy backbone and align therapy representation with CodeableReference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 child names and `medication[x]` choice while broadening definitions and targets.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Reusing a common other-therapy backbone and broadening therapy targets are reasonable goals, but the R4 shape already had a concept-or-reference choice that could have been evolved. Renaming `therapyRelationshipType` and replacing `medication[x]` with `treatment` appears more avoidable than necessary, especially because retaining a nonoptimal old name is a legitimate compatibility tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]`, clarified that the medication field covers other treatments in this context, and broadened or renamed target profiles such as MedicinalProductDefinition and SubstanceDefinition. This would meet most of the R6 modeling goal with moderate naming debt, without adding a duplicate same-resource field for the same fact.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves a nonideal `medication` name for broader treatments but avoids most wire-format and generated-accessor breakage.

evidence.detail: R4 has `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]`.
R6 contraindication.otherTherapy reuses the indication.otherTherapy backbone with renamed children and CodeableReference treatment.

examples.examplesMd: R4 `medicationCodeableConcept` maps to `treatment.concept`; R4 `medicationReference` maps to `treatment.reference` if the target is valid or can be migrated.

findings.narrativeMd: `otherTherapy` survives conceptually but its generated accessors and JSON children change. This is a high-risk area for automated converters because it combines renaming, choice-type removal, CodeableReference wrapping, and target-profile migration.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `otherTherapy.medicationCodeableConcept` or `medicationReference` elements are not valid R6 elements. R6 treatments referencing targets newly allowed in R6 are not losslessly representable in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `therapyRelationshipType` to `relationshipType`. Map `medicationCodeableConcept` to `treatment.concept`; map `medicationReference` to `treatment.reference` after target resource migration. Review references to R4 `Substance` and `SubstanceSpecification`, which need a target strategy for R6 `SubstanceDefinition` or another allowed type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less-breaking design could have retained the old choice element and target set while adding new aliases. The R6 model instead prefers a common CodeableReference pattern, which is cleaner but not wire-compatible.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `otherTherapy` backbone keeps the same broad concept but changes child names from `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]` to `relationshipType` and `treatment`, while also switching the treatment value to `CodeableReference` with changed targets. The CodeableReference wrapping and target updates have an R6 modeling rationale, but the child-name changes look substantially avoidable: R4 already had a concept-or-reference choice for the therapy. For a safety-relevant conditional-therapy relationship, preserving old wire names or a transitional alias appears to have lower cost than many other alternatives.
keyEvidence: R4 `otherTherapy.therapyRelationshipType`: `1..1 CodeableConcept`.
R4 `otherTherapy.medication[x]`: `1..1 CodeableConcept|Reference(MedicinalProduct|Medication|Substance|SubstanceSpecification)`.
R6 `indication.otherTherapy.relationshipType`: `1..1 CodeableConcept` with preferred therapy-relationship-type binding.

R6 `indication.otherTherapy.treatment`: `1..1 CodeableReference(MedicinalProductDefinition|Medication|SubstanceDefinition|NutritionProduct|BiologicallyDerivedProduct|ActivityDefinition)`; contraindication reuses that backbone by contentReference.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the compatibility bar, but this path can affect generated APIs and conditional contraindication logic. The apparent low-cost name-preservation option keeps the concern above the threshold for Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 child names and choice-element names are not valid R6 child names; runtime/API/codegen also changes generated accessors and target-resource handling.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]` while broadening definitions and targets, or accepted aliases during transition. The tradeoff is semantic naming debt because `medication` is narrower than `treatment`, but that seems modest compared with breaking both wire names and accessors.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing assessment that a less-breaking base design is available; the fresh review still recognizes the low FMM but finds the rename portion insufficiently justified.

findings.title: population changes from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could inline population criteria such as age, gender, race, and physiological condition via the `Population` complex type.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 points to `Group` resources instead of carrying the R4 inline `Population` datatype.

facts.note: Cardinality did not materially change, but representation did.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements describe the population group to which the clinical-use information applies.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The R4 inline complex value is invalid at the R6 location, which expects references. Migration may require creating or reusing `Group` resources and preserving old inline criteria. Down-conversion from a Group reference requires dereferencing and may lose Group identity or complex membership criteria.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Population qualifiers often determine whether a contraindication applies to pediatric, pregnant, sex-specific, or physiologic subgroups.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent populations through the general Group resource rather than a specialized inline Population type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep inline Population and add a Group reference option for reusable populations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using `Group` can improve reuse and align population criteria with a general resource, but the available package evidence does not explain why inline `Population` had to be removed. The break forces creation or discovery of Group resources and can be lossy, so the breakage is not clearly justified without stronger rationale.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the inline `Population` element and added an optional `Reference(Group)` element for reusable or externally maintained populations. This is only partial because duplicate inline and referenced population criteria can diverge, and the deprecated inline representation might persist indefinitely, but it would preserve R4 population-bearing instances better than a reference-only model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 inline criteria but creates two population representations and extra validation and reconciliation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 population is type Population.
R4 Population contains inline criteria such as age, gender, race, and physiological condition.
R6 population is Reference(Group).

examples.examplesMd: The migration example assumes a corresponding Group resource has been created or identified.

findings.narrativeMd: `population` changes from embedded criteria to a resource reference. This has broad runtime implications because converters must create, find, or reference `Group` resources and decide how to preserve inline criteria and identifiers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 inline `Population` object is not valid in R6. An R6 `Reference(Group)` is not representable in R4 without dereferencing to criteria that fit the old Population datatype or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a population migration strategy before bulk conversion. For each R4 Population, create a Group or map to an existing Group, store traceability to the original inline criteria, and test age, gender, race, and physiological-condition examples. For down-conversion, decide whether Group references can be dereferenced or must be flagged as lossy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A `population[x]` choice or transitional extension would have preserved old inline values. The R6 design favors reuse of Group but shifts burden to migration and reference management.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed population criteria inline with the `Population` datatype, while R6 requires references to `Group` resources. This can be a hard wire-format break and a modeling break: migration may need to create or identify a `Group`, preserve inline age/sex/race/physiological-condition criteria, and decide how to handle Group identity and membership rules on down-conversion. Population qualifiers often determine whether a contraindication applies, so the lossiness and operational burden are not erased by low FMM.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication.population`: `0..* Population`.
R4 `Population` contains inline `age[x]`, `gender`, `race`, and `physiologicalCondition` elements.
R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.population`: `0..* Reference(Group)`.
Public IDMP context checked: clinical-use data is framed as regulatory and patient-safety relevant, but no verified production dependency on this exact population shape was found.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens stability expectations, but this path can be central to safe applicability of contraindications and migration can require expert modeling choices rather than a simple syntactic transform.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an inline R4 `Population` object is not a valid R6 `Reference(Group)`; R6-to-R4 loss occurs unless the referenced Group can be dereferenced and expressed in the old Population datatype.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have allowed `population[x]` or retained inline Population while adding Group references. That creates duplicate population representations and reconciliation burden, but it would preserve old criteria and reduce the need to mint external Group resources.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high impact and partial alternative assessment; the fresh review treats this as Revisit because the change is potentially lossy and expert-dependent despite FMM 0.

findings.title: R6 adds modifier status with no R4 counterpart

oldState.summary: No local status/modifier element on R4 MedicinalProductContraindication.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 contraindication instances had no local lifecycle/status element that could mark the record as retired or otherwise not valid.

newState.summary: Optional CodeableConcept status is a modifier and summary element.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` can alter whether the clinical-use definition should be treated as current/valid.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is a new local element on the R6 successor resource, not an inherited base change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element is optional, so it does not make R4 data invalid when converting to R6. It is nevertheless a high runtime risk for R6 consumers and down-converters because modifier elements cannot be ignored safely, and R4 has no local place to carry this status.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Using a retired or invalid contraindication as if it were current can create safety and regulatory risk.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent lifecycle state for clinical-use definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional R6 status is not an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` is optional for R4-to-R6 migration and provides a first-class modifier for lifecycle state that can affect safe use of clinical knowledge. The compatibility issue is that R4 has no equivalent local field when converting R6 content back, not that R4-valid instances are rejected by R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed for the R4-to-R6 direction because R4 instances can omit this optional element. R4 extensions or sidecar metadata may mitigate down-conversion loss, but those are migration/backport strategies rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining concern is lossy R6-to-R4 down-conversion, not a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 status is 0..1 CodeableConcept, isModifier true, with preferred publication-status binding.
No local R4 status element exists on MedicinalProductContraindication.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates status semantics that should not be silently dropped when down-converting.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a lifecycle status with modifier semantics. This is not a forward-validation break for R4 data, but it is a significant runtime and down-conversion risk because status can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 conversion can omit `status` and remain valid. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot preserve this local modifier without an extension or external metadata, and consumers that ignore it may use obsolete clinical-use content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Teach R6 clients to inspect `ClinicalUseDefinition.status`. For down-conversion, map status to a standard extension or sidecar metadata and make consumers aware that dropping it is lossy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A status extension could have supported older resources, but the R6 model benefits from a first-class modifier element that validators and generated code can surface.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` as a modifier, with no local R4 counterpart. This is not a forward validation break for R4 data, but it matters for R6-to-R4 conversion because dropping a status such as retired can change whether a contraindication should be used. The R6 design is still proportionate: lifecycle state is important enough to be first-class and modifier-marked rather than hidden in extensions.
keyEvidence: No local R4 `status` element exists on `MedicinalProductContraindication`.
R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.status`: `0..1 CodeableConcept`, preferred `publication-status` binding, `isModifier = true`.

freshReview.fmmEffect: The old artifact's FMM 0 status reduces any expectation that R6 must backport a local status-compatible shape. Safety relevance explains why the modifier matters, but it supports the R6 addition rather than a Revisit judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: optional R6 status can carry lifecycle semantics that R4 has no local field to preserve; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break is introduced by this optional element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for the forward direction. R4 extensions or sidecar metadata can mitigate down-conversion, but those are migration/backport strategies rather than reasons to avoid the R6 element.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies no hard forward break and high reverse/modifier risk; the fresh judgment frames the change as proportionate rather than a design problem.

findings.title: R6 introduces local terminology bindings where R4 had none

oldState.summary: No local bindings on R4 contraindication-specific CodeableConcept fields.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 StructureDefinition did not bind `disease`, `diseaseStatus`, `comorbidity`, `otherTherapy.therapyRelationshipType`, or `otherTherapy.medication[x]` locally.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Bindings were compared on the R4 elements and their mapped R6 successor elements.

impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Terminology guidance for contraindication conditions and therapy relationships can affect clinical decision support consistency.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide terminology guidance for clinical-use content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: example and preferred bindings do not invalidate base R4-coded content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding non-required terminology guidance is a reasonable way to improve interoperability without creating a hard base validation break. Because the bindings are example or preferred rather than required, the base R6 design already avoids rejecting legacy codes solely for non-membership.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no meaningful less-breaking base alternative to calibrate because the R6 bindings are guidance-level. Implementers may need terminology mapping when local profiles strengthen these bindings, but that is a profile or migration concern rather than a base R6 backward-compatible alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low base-conformance risk; stricter downstream profiles or UI policies may still require terminology migration.

evidence.detail: R4 local contraindication elements have no local terminology bindings.
R6 adds example/preferred bindings on mapped fields.

evidence.sourceRef: R6 ValueSet-disease-symptom-procedure, ValueSet-disease-status, ValueSet-therapy-relationship-type, ValueSet-therapy, ValueSet-interaction-management
evidence.detail: Several R6 bindings use SNOMED-based compose filters or HL7 code systems; expansions were not compared.

findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not treat these bindings as required during base R4-to-R6 migration. Where local profiles require tighter conformance, run terminology validation and maintain a mapping policy for existing codes. SNOMED-based bindings need terminology-server support for reliable expansion checks.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The bindings are appropriately non-required for base compatibility. The main risk comes from downstream implementation choices rather than the base StructureDefinition alone.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansions were not performed; impact may increase in jurisdictions or profiles that require these value sets.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds example and preferred bindings for several mapped contraindication fields. These bindings can influence UI pick lists, generated hints, terminology QA, or stricter derived profiles, but they do not make base R4 codes invalid in R6. For the base StructureDefinition comparison, this is useful interoperability guidance rather than a material compatibility break.

R6 condition/status/comorbidity/treatment bindings are example strength; `otherTherapy.relationshipType` and some metadata bindings are preferred strength.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional added R6 elements do not break R4-to-R6 base validation.

They do not require old R4 instances to change in order to validate after the main structural migration.

Standard extensions or external metadata may be useful when representing R6-only content in R4, but those are down-conversion mitigations, not backward-compatible alternatives to the R6 base model.

evidence.detail: R6 defines new optional elements around the contraindication branch.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional fields such as `identifier`, `category`, `contraindication.management`, `contraindication.applicability`, and `library`. They do not make R4-to-R6 migration fail, but R6-to-R4 conversion can lose identifiers, management advice, applicability logic, and computable library links if a system round-trips through R4. freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use means old R4 compatibility should not block optional R6 expressivity. The safety relevance of management/applicability mainly affects migration policy, not the base design judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: optional R6-only metadata and logic have no standard local R4 destination; no old-valid/new-invalid forward break is introduced.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for optional additions. Extensions, sidecar artifacts, or explicit down-conversion loss flags are appropriate mitigations, but not base-model alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing no-hard-break and not-applicable alternative assessment; the fresh review keeps the reverse-loss warning but treats the base design as proportionate.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: After mapping locations, the optional/repeating cardinalities for disease-like fields, comorbidity, therapeutic indication/indication, otherTherapy, and population remain broadly 0..1 or 0..* as in R4. The material cardinality break is separately reported for `subject` and the new required `type` discriminator.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Successor artifact maturity/status differs
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 resource is draft/trial-use FMM 0 while R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` is active with normative standards-status and FMM 2 in the package metadata. This affects governance expectations but is not itself an instance validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat this as a signal that the successor model may be more stable and broader than the R4 trial-use medicinal-product resource family.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds business identifiers
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `identifier` is optional, so R4 instances do not need it to validate in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: If R4 systems used external identifiers outside the resource, R6 provides a first-class place to carry them.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds category for clinical-use issue grouping
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `category` is optional with a preferred binding, so it does not invalidate migrated R4 records.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Category may improve presentation and regulatory organization, but down-conversion to R4 needs an extension or sidecar field.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 can reference logic libraries
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `library` is optional and therefore not a forward compatibility break for R4 data.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: If R6 contraindications use computable logic, R4 representations may need extensions or external logic references to preserve behavior.
